questions.question: Explain why human gametes contain 23 chromosomes and not 46.
questions.expected_answer: Body cells have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs. Gametes carry one chromosome from each pair, 23 in total, so that when a sperm and an egg fuse at fertilisation the zygote has 23 + 23, which is 46 chromosomes, the normal number. If gametes had 46, the chromosome number would double every generation.

questions.question: Name the organ where each of the following happens: sperm production, egg release, fertilisation, development of the baby.
questions.expected_answer: Sperm production: the testes. Egg release: the ovaries. Fertilisation: the oviduct (Fallopian tube). Development of the baby: the uterus.

questions.question: Describe two health issues of the reproductive system and how each can be prevented or treated.
questions.expected_answer: Any two, for example: sexually transmitted infections, prevented by abstinence or condoms, with bacterial infections such as syphilis cured by antibiotics and viral ones such as HIV controlled by medication; cervical cancer, caused by HPV, prevented by the HPV vaccine and detected early by Pap smears; infertility, caused by blocked tubes, hormone problems or low sperm count and worsened by smoking and alcohol, prevented partly by treating infections early and healthy living; testicular cancer, detected early by monthly self-examination.
